messages:
Sam Caldwell: I'm about to handoff, wrapping up a slow degradation on /generate. Primary -> Anya. brief notes below.
Anya Patel: taking primary. thanks Sam. any known customer impact right now?
Sam Caldwell: impact: 5% of requests hit high-tail latency (>2s) for embeddings route, some timeouts for small workloads. No error 5xx spike. we've routed affected traffic to a slower variant (gpt-embed-small-v2) via the routing policy.
Mike H.: noted. Are we patched in routing policy or is that a manual toggle?
Sam Caldwell: manual roll to fallback policy in console (Console -> Routing -> project:redwood-prod -> fallback: gpt-embed-small-v2). I left the change annotated in the audit log.
Anya Patel: ok taking notes. primary/secondary for next 8h: Primary=Anya, Secondary=Mike H. escalation to oncall-sre if page persists >30m.
Tara Nguyen: I can cover backups if both of you get paged. leaving at 22:00 UTC, so will be reachable for handover until then.
incident-bot: [INCIDENT] Pager triggered: embeddings-latency-high - severity: P2 - triggered at 1977654100 by latency threshold 95th>1500ms. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings_latency
Mike H.: quick checks I did: node CPU and GPU metrics look normal, KV cache hit-rate dropped ~30% at 1977653500. suspect cache eviction or stale entries.
Anya Patel: KV cache drop could explain tail latency. Sam, did we rotate any config for cache TTL?
Sam Caldwell: not in last 24h. but I bounced a cache-worker yesterday morning. see ops note: "restarted cache-worker pool for memory leak mitigation". Might have wiped in-memory prewarm.
Tara Nguyen: suggested quick fixes in order: 1) warm cache by running the cache prewarm job, 2) if that fails, rollback restart or redeploy cache-worker to previous image, 3) enable target routing weight to fallback model for 10m.
Anya Patel: can someone run prewarm now? what's the job name?
Mike H.: job is `jobs/prewarm-embeddings-cache` in k8s namespace redwood-prod. command: `kubectl -n redwood-prod create job --from=cronjob/prewarm-embeddings-cache prewarm-manual-$(date +%s)`
Tara Nguyen: +1 run that. also keep an eye on cost; prewarm can spike GPU util if it triggers model loads.
Sam Caldwell: I kicked prewarm at 1977654345. logs: first batch completed, cache hit-rate back to ~68% from 42% after ~3m. latency 95th dropped to ~900ms (prewarm still warming).
Anya Patel: nice. can we annotate the incident with customer-facing guidance?
Mike H.: Suggested status blurb: "We are observing elevated latency for embeddings requests. We've activated a temporary fallback to a lower-capacity model and are warming cache; most requests should see improved latency within minutes. No data loss. We're monitoring and will update in 30 minutes."
Tara Nguyen: pinging support channel with that blurb now. https://redwood.internal/docs/status-template (used).
incident-bot: [UPDATE] Ticket INC-4821 linked. Attachments: diag/kv-drop-1977654300.png
Sam Caldwell: followups for handoff: - runbook links I used: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv_cache_restore ; https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rollback-deploy ; https://redwood.internal/runbooks/traffic-routing-weighting ; - quick commands: `kubectl -n redwood-prod get pods -l app=cache-worker -o wide` and `kubectl -n redwood-prod logs deploy/cache-worker -c prewarm`
Anya Patel: copying those into handoff doc. Coverage gaps: if prewarm fails and fallback model is saturated, we may need to open a temporary capacity burst or contact capacity team. How quickly can we toggle autoscale?
Mike H.: autoscale policy change is immediate but provisioning GPUs can take 4-12 minutes depending on region. We should only request burst if latency doesn't improve in 20m.
Tara Nguyen: escalation checklist for secondary: 1) verify KV cache state; 2) confirm routing fallback is active; 3) run prewarm job; 4) if no improvement, increase routing weight to fallback to 80%; 5) file priority capacity request with sz:medium.
Anya Patel: I updated the runbook pointer in the console to include the new cache-prewarm step. Also left a note in audit: "handed primary to Anya at 1977654321, cache prewarm kicked, monitoring".
Sam Caldwell: leaving now. Anya, Mike, ping me if anything spikes. :wave:
Anya Patel: thanks Sam. I'll update incident every 10m and close the thread when 95th < 600ms for 30m.
Mike H.: adding quick remediation snippets for future handoffs to the runbook: - if KV miss spike: `curl -X POST https://internal-api/redwood/prewarm -d '{"model":"embed-v2","warm":true}'` - if routing needs manual: `redwoodctl route set --project prod --route embeddings --model gpt-embed-small-v2 --weight 80`
Tara Nguyen: tagging the ticket for postmortem if we hit a customer SLA breach. otherwise we'll include a short entry in weekly ops notes. :memo:
ops-bot: Scheduled reminder: oncall-handoff-checklist at 1977654700
Anya Patel: acknowledged. will follow the checklist and solicit any outstanding questions before 1977654780.
Mike H.: monitoring metrics dashboard link: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/embeddings-latency (shared).
incident-bot: [RESOLVE] Incident embeddings-latency-high marked as resolved at 1977654760 - cause: cache warm loss after worker restart - remediation: cache prewarm, routing fallback.
Anya Patel: resolving now. final note for handoff: Primary=Anya, Secondary=Mike until 04:00 UTC; customer impact contained, no SLA breach. Closing. :white_check_mark:
Tara Nguyen: thanks team, great handoff.
__notes: Generated synthetic Slack thread for eng-oncall handoff and incident coordination. All URLs and timestamps are fictitious.
